Last SetNext() call should set that flag to true, which means that no more data will be set, and the actual processing of the CBOR data buffer can be initiated.

Get the matching Attribute(s), and provides the result into a CBOR encoded buffer. The caller of this function provides the "filter" in a "specified" CBOR structure. This means that the caller can provide a more advanced filter than in the "normal" Get() function. The CBOR structure supported is a list of lists, with the following format (using '{' '}' to denote optional parameters); < specified > := [ < attributes > ] < attributes > := ( < attribute > | < attributes > ) < attribute > := [ < familyId > {, < attributeId > {, < attributeIndex } } ] < familyId > := ** uint16 ** < attributeId > := ** uint16 ** < attributeIndex > := ** uint32 **.
Same as GetSpecified, but request is larger than can be sent in a single request.
Function used after a GetSpecified, to provide more data until endOfData is set to true.
Same as GetSpecified, but request data is fetched from a Raw Attribute.

Sets one single "large" attribute. In case this call doesn't end the data, SetNext() shall be used (see Set() for details).
Same as the GetRaw() function, but gets the checksum.
Same as Get, but possible to control if Raw Attributes should be fetched.
Same as GetSpecified, but possible to control if Raw Attributes should be fetched.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
Authentication handles communication authentication. It implements a number of different types of login procedures, and a number of login levels.

## Login levels/roles
The following levels are defined:

##### None
No login has been performed.

##### Operator
An operator has logged in. An operator is the regular user of the product, and usually logs in using a pin code. However, it is also possible to login as operator using an authentication procedure, with a private key.

##### Service
Service login is used by AutoCheck, in production etc. This level unlocks certain commands that may disable some safety features etc in order to be able to test the product. It does not unlock features that makes the product vulnerable for theft etc.

Only available through authentication procedure using private key.

##### Advanced
Unlocks commands that may be used to reconfigure the product.

Only available through authentication procedure using private key.

##### Super
Unlocks everything...

## Block protection
After a number of failed login attempts, the system will be blocked for further login attempts for a while. When the blocking is released, one more attempt is accepted. If that fails, the system is blocked again for a longer time. And so on.

A block is global, so all types of logins will be blocked, not only the type that caused the blocking. Also, successful login on one type does not reset the failed attempt counters on the other types.

Currently, the system is blocked for 5 minutes after 5 failed attempts. After each fail the blocking time is doubled, until a maximum of 160 minutes.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
The Calendar handles mowing tasks. Use this module to control at what times and what week days the mower shall be active.

## Task handling
Tasks can be added, modified and deleted. They are accessed using task indexes, which will always be in and uninterrupted range from 0 to number of tasks.

Note! An index of a task is not constant, if a task is deleted the other tasks may have updated indexes. I.e., there is no point in remembering an index of a task for later usage, since it may have been updated.

## Task transaction
If several modifications to the Calendar shall be done at one instance, a transaction shall be used. After a call to StartTransactions, all modifications are done in a sand box until CommitTransaction is performed. If a transaction is not used for 2s, it is discarded.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
The Fota family encapsulates the Firmware Over The Air transfer and installation process. Fota follows the following state flow.

![Fota states](https://lucid.app/documents/image/a0d0adb0-9786-4f30-973a-5a38d42b8cb7/0/500)

The mower will connect once every week to check for new software. If available, the download will start. During download, the mower will be restricted from mowing, to ensure stable transfer. The transfer can be paused for various reasons, such as a forced start from the user.

##### Forcing a check for updates
The one week periodicity can be overridden with Fota.CheckForUpdates(), which will trigger a check immediately.

##### Applying an update
When the full software has been transferred to the mower, Fota.ApplyUpdate() triggers the installation. Fota will change state to Installing SW before the installation starts. During the installation, the mower will disconnect from all communication, and may restart several times. When the installation is completed, the mower will restart and return to the same mower state as it was in before the update. The Fota state will go back to idle.

##### Automatic updates
Automatic updates can be enabled using Fota.SetAutoFotaEnabled(). The mower will automatically install an update when it is suitable, for instance when the mower is in the charging station and the battery level is high enough. Before the installation is automatically triggered, the state AUTOMATIC_INSTALLATION_PENDING is active.

The mower is also updated automatically when System.SwUpdateRequired is set. It will automatically check for an update, and automatically install it when completely downloaded. In this case, the only prerequisite is that the battery is not very low, no other conditions need to be met. If the battery is too low, the state AUTOMATIC_INSTALLATION_PENDING will be active in the same way as for regular automatic updates.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
### Behavior description The __Autotimer__ adjusts the operating times so that a uniform cutting result is achieved within the operating period allowed by the calendar (considering actual grass growth and seasonal changes). * If grass growth is increased, the present average current consumption will be higher than the reference, the results of the __Autotimer__ will be increased and the mower will mow more (until limited by __Calender__ or __Autotimer__). When next calendar task starts, the reference level will be increased. * If grass growth is decreased, the present average current consumption will be lower than the reference, the results of the __Autotimer__ will be decreased and the mower will mow less (until limited by __Autotimer__). When next calendar task starts, the reference level will be decreased. #### Input * __Current consumption__ - The current consumption (in mA) for the Blade motor, expressed as an average over the latest 5 seconds * __Tasks__ - Tasks from __Calendar__ module (each task may have one or more cutting cycles) #### Output * Restriction reason (_No reason_ or _Autotimer limit_)
Note: This will be used as input to the __MowerApp__ for decision on whether continued mowing is allowed or not. The __Autotimer__ module has no knowledge of the other modules that make actual decisions on mowing restriction.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
The mower contains a number of central application modules, MowerApp, Planner and Calendar. The MowerApp is the module that does the actual work, and it would like to do it as much as possible. The Planner, however, has a broader perspective and decides if it is actually a good idea to be mowing right now. It uses the Calendar for organization, and restrictor modules such as the AutoTimer and the FrostSensor that may have an opinion about this.

All planning ends up in a mission to perform. What the mission can be depends on the mower model. The simplest mission is mission 0, default mission, which is usually just mowing the garden that is specified with a standard loop wire. More advanced missions can be systematic mowing missions using high resolution positioning system. In those cases, the SiteMap is used to hold the map of the garden.

![Mower modules](https://lucid.app/documents/image/43f77054-a789-4e66-8772-e2b3c5242a0c/0/2000)

## MowerApp
MowerApp is a high level interface to the mower application. It handles overall state of the mower, defines the different modes of
operation, and gives information about current activity of the mower.

## Mode of operation
##### Auto / main area
- Mower will mow until low battery. Go home and charge. Leave and continue mowing.
- Week schedule is used.
- Schedule can be overridden with forced park or forced mowing.

##### Demo mode
- Same as main area, but shorter times.
- No blade operation.

##### Home mode
- Mower goes home and parks forever.
- Week schedule is not used.
- Cannot be overridden with forced mowing.

##### Manual / secondary area
- Mower will mow until empty battery, or a limited time. When done, it stops in the garden.
- Week schedule is not used.
- Cannot be overridden with forced park.
- If a forced park override timer is set, mower stops when that timer runs out.

## Mower states
The mower states define the overall state of the mower.

![Mower state diagram](https://lucid.app/documents/image/797ec7e4-cf46-4bc2-838b-1e7ce52977a8/0/2000)

##### Off
Mower is turned off

##### WaitForSafetyPin
Mower is waiting for a pin code, for safety reasons. Until a correct pin code is entered, the internal safety supervisor will not allow any operation.

A user can use Authentication.IsTrustedToEnterSafetyPin to understand if a pin code can be entered using his connection. If yes, a pin code view can be displayed, otherwise there is no point.

##### Stopped
Mower is stopped, and cannot be started remotely. Start requirements (safety or other) are not fulfilled.

##### Fatal error
A fatal error has occured. Error has to be fixed confirmed to leave this state.

##### Check Safety
Mower is waiting for safety requirements to be fulfilled. Typically, on a mower with a hatch, it is waiting for the hatch to be closed after start command has been issued.

##### In Operation
Mower is operating according to selected mode. The activity gives information about what it is currently up to.

##### Restricted
The mower is currently restricted from mowing for some reason. It will continue mowing when the restriction is removed. The activity gives information about what the mower is currently up to.

##### Error
A temporary error has occured. If the error is resolved, the mower will resume operation without user interaction. Typically, this happens when the loop signal is lost. When it comes back, the operation is resumes.

## Activities
When the mower is in the state In Operation or Restricted, it is operating according to the selected mode. In these states, the mower reports an activity that describes what the mower is currently doing.

No functionality shall be build upon the activities, other than displaying for the user what the mower is up to.

![Mower activites](https://lucid.app/documents/image/797ec7e4-cf46-4bc2-838b-1e7ce52977a8/2/2000)

##### Going out
Mower is currently leaving the charging station and is heading out to a starting point.

##### Mowing
Mower is currently mowing.

##### Going home
Mower is currently going home to the charging station.

##### Charging
Mower is currently charging. Note that the mower will only report the activity charging if it was its own decision to go home and charge. I.e., it would like to mow but is charging because it has to. If the mower is restricted it may very well charge when in the charging station, but the activity will be Parked.

For detailed information about the actual charging status, use the Battery interface.

##### Parked
Mower is parked in the charging station.

##### Stopped in garden
Mower has stopped in garden, for instance in manual mode when the task has been completed.

## Inactive reason
There are situations when the mower looks inactive to the user, even though there is no error. In those scenarios, the inactive reason informs about the reason for why the mower is standing still. The inactive reason may show information whenever the mower is expected to be doing something, which means in state IN_OPERATION or RESTRICTED. It can be reported in any activity.

Typical inactive reasons are:

- Searching for satellites. Waiting for fix when using EPOS.
- Planning. The mower is planning a path or a systematic mission.

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
The Planner is responsible for what the mower should be doing at the moment. It takes into consideration the tasks in Calendar, but it also considers restrictions due to Autotimer, Frost sensor and other things. ## Main purpose The outcome of the Planner is a decision on whether the MowerApp shall be allowed to mow, or if it should be restricted. If it shall mow, the Planner also gives the MowerApp a mission. If it is restricted, the Planner provides information about why it made that decision. ## Override concept The Planner has an override feature, which can be used to override the operation decided by the Calendar. There is room for one override at a time, and it occurs from now and for a duration of time. I.e., there is no way to schedule an override in the future. ### Override mow SetOverrideMow or SetOverrideMowMission will force the mower to mow for the specified amount of time. When the time has elapsed, the override is removed and the Planner reverts to the Calendar instead. If the selected mission is a mission that can be completed, such as a systematic mission, the override will be removed when that happens. An override can be set to last forever, if the duration is set to 0. Note that this does not apply to the case of a mission that can be completed, as described above.
SetOverrideMowSetOverrideMowMission
EPOS - Auto mode Will iterate through all missions for the specified time. Mows selected mission, either for the specified time or until completed (for systematic missions).
EPOS - Manual mode Not allowed Mows selected mission for the specified time, or until empty battery. Stops in garden when completed.
LONA - Auto mode Mows "my lawn" for the specified time Mows selected mission for the specified time
- Only allowed for enabled missions
- Only allowed if Lona state is MAP_READY.
LONA - Manual mode Mows wherever the mower is located, for the specified time or until empty battery. Lona map is not used. Not allowed (except for mission id = 0, which is the same as calling SetOverrideMow).
### Override park SetOverridePark and SetOverrideParkUntilNextStart will force the mower to park for a specified amount of time. When the time has elapsed, the override is removed and the Planner reverts to the Calendar. Override park until next start means that no more mowing will be done within the current task. Operation will be resumed at the start of the next task instead. If this is issued when there is no current task, it is accepted but becomes rather pointless. ## Restricted When the mower app is in the state Restricted, the Planner can explain why. It can also inform about when operation will be resumed again, with the GetNextStartTime command. This is only valid when the mower is restricted. The Planner will select one of the active restriction reasons as the "public" reason. It is provides two lists of restrictions, where all active restrictions are listed. ### Internal and external restrictions There are a number of restrictions that are detected by the mower itself. These are called internal restrictions. In addition, external systems can restrict the mower, called external restrictions. There are two lists, restrictions and external restrictions. If one or more external restrictions are active, there is an entry in the list of internal restrictions called external. This means that there is always at least one entry in the internal restrictions list when the mower is restricted. ### Restriction reasons ##### Week schedule There is no task in the Calendar right now, nothing to do. ##### Park override The restriction is because someone forced us to park, using the override feature. ##### Autotimer The Autotimer has decided that the grass is short enough, so there is no need to wear it down even more. This restriction reason is often referred to as Sensor restriction, but it is only used by the Autotimer. ##### Daily limit If a model has a maximum allowed mowing time per day, this restriction will apply when that time has run out. ##### Fota (Cloud synchronization) When a Fota update is being transferred to the mower, we want to remain in the charging station to ensure that the transfer is successful. The restriction is removed when the transfer is done. **Note!** The Fota restriction is also used when the mower is transferring data for Lona maps calculation, and other synching with Robotics backend. The name "Fota" for this restriction is therefore no longer applicable, but is kept for backwards compatibility. ##### Frost sensor The frost sensor thinks it is too cold to mow. ##### All missions completed If the Calendar allows operation of one or more missions right now, but they are all completed, the Planner will restrict the mower from mowing simply because there is nothing more to do. ##### External One or more external restrictions are currently active. ## Mission prioritization When several missions are available at a specific time, the Planner uses the following prio to decide which mission to choose: - If an override is active, the mission is specified by the override. - If already performing a mission, don't change until it is completed. - If a mission was not fully completed last time it was performed, select it in favor of missions that were fully completed. - When choosing between two missions that were fully completed last time, select the one that was completed least recent. - Do not run the same mission more than once a day (applies only to systematic missions). - Do not run the same mission more than once each task (applies only to systematic missions).

documentations.name: Public
documentations.description:
The Clock module provides an interface for time settings in the system. The system uses local time internally, i.e. the time at the place where the machine is (machine time). It can operate without knowing time zone and time offset etc. The time zone and time offset shall be set by an external system (backend or app), and can be used to understand the mower's time in relation to global time. It can also be used to automatically sync the time of the mower, if the auto sync setting is enabled.

The mower will never change offset or time zone by itself. The autosync is handled by backend, including changing of the offset due to daylight saving. If time zone is not set, no automatic updates will be done.

Time zone is an ascii string on the TZ format, for example Europe/Stockholm. The offset compared to UTC time in seconds, for instance +1h for Stockholm (3600s).
